---
description: "Use when building or modifying React components, app layout, controls, styling, or accessibility."
applyTo:
  - "src/components/**"
  - "src/App.tsx"
  - "src/App.css"
  - "src/index.css"
---
# React UI Instructions

- Use function components and the existing game/settings contexts. Dispatch game actions for shared state changes; do not duplicate blackjack rules in components.
- Use Fluent UI v9 components and design tokens, following nearby component and styling patterns. Do not hard-code colors; use `tokens` in `makeStyles` or the theme's CSS variables in stylesheets, so components follow the theme mode and accent chosen in the Appearance settings.
- Appearance settings (theme mode, accent, card style, card back pattern and color) are typed keys of `SettingsState` with their allowed values in `settingOptions`. Add new presets to `src/theme/` and keep the Options panel controls to stock Fluent components.
- Preserve accessible names for interactive controls with labels or `aria-label`; retain useful tooltip relationships and keyboard-operable controls.
- There is no splash screen. Before a game, `src/components/Table.tsx` shows the selected players and the dealer as floating seat chips, the dealer first and tagged "Dealer", and starts play with the Start game button in the dock. Do not reintroduce splash-screen visibility settings or a separate player-selection start dialog.
- The Players dialog in `src/components/PlayersDialog.tsx` is opened from the header. It creates named profiles, selects the human profile for the next game, and shows profile statistics; a roster change never touches a hand in play: it is seated through the `SetRoster` action, which the reducer ignores until the round is settled. Between hands App applies it at once; a change made during play is applied by the Next hand button (or the Options panel's Deal) before dealing. When a hand ends, the action toolbar in the dock is replaced by a primary Next hand button (styled like Start game) and a secondary Change players button; Change players opens the same dialog through `PlayersDialogContext`, which App provides.
- The Table has three seat areas, with no headings. Seats that are not on the stage wait as `SeatChip`s in the reverse of turn order, the dealer, who plays last, first and the human, who plays first, last. Seats still to play wait above the stage (`.table-waiting`), the next to play closest to it; the seat in control, or one the user clicked, expands on the stage (`.table-focus`) as a `PlayerContainer`; a seat whose turn is over moves to just below the stage (`.table-played`), ahead of those that played before it, so the first to play ends at the bottom. When the round is over nobody has the stage (`turnKey` in `Table.tsx` does not fall back to the human), so every seat is below it, dealer first and human last; the layout gets `is-stageless` and, on a wide board, one centered column. The next deal sends the seats back to their places. While each seat's result is told in the toasts (`useTableToasts` returns `focus`), its chip is in focus: `SeatChip`'s `focus` prop makes it pulse, brighten and ring in the result's color, with a static brightness and ring under reduced motion. `seatQueues` in `src/functions/round.ts` (with `seatOrder`) works out the two lists; do not derive turn order in components. The dealer's chip has no heading: `seatTag` in `src/functions/seatStatus.ts` gives it one tag naming its role and status ("Dealer · Waiting", "Dealer · Playing", its result). A dealer that was waiting when the round ended stays above the stage until its hole card has turned over and a pause (`CARD_REVEAL_PAUSE_MS`, at least a second) has passed, so the flip and the hand are seen. On a board at least 720px wide the seats are a column of a third at the side chosen by the `queueSide` setting (left by default), the waiting seats at the top of it and the played seats at the bottom, with the stage beside both; before a game, with no stage, the chips float together in the middle. Below that the board is one column (waiting seats, stage, played seats) and chips are compact full-width rows. `useSeatFlip` animates slots (`data-seat-key`, `data-seat-role` of `waiting`, `played` or `focus`) when they change role or place; it measures layout offsets, so `.table-board` must stay a positioned ancestor of the slots. The staged seat gets visual focus only; keyboard focus stays with the dock's buttons.
- The dock (`.table-dock`) is one row along the board's bottom edge, sticky to the bottom of the window: the pot, then the game's buttons, then the activity log button. Keep it to one row at every width. Its middle shows Start game before a game, `ControlPanel` for the human (the action toolbar, or Next hand and Change players once the hand ends), and "<name> is playing" during a computer seat's turn. Game buttons belong in the dock, not in a seat; the pre-deal wager hint is the exception and stays in the human's staged seat. The toolbar collapses to icons from the `dock-actions` container query in `Table.css`.
- The pot stays at the start of the dock before, during and after a hand; do not move it around the table. `usePotMotion` slides the last pot up out of its slot and the new one in from the top when a hand or game begins, and shimmers and bounces it when it grows; the controls and dealer automation wait through `PotAnimationContext` until it finishes. With reduced motion there is no bounce and no wait.
- The page shell in `src/App.tsx` is a flex column at least as tall as the window, and the Table (`.table-shell` and `.table-board`) grows to fill the height below the header, shrinking when the activity drawer opens but never below its content. The table sits `PAGE_GUTTER` (`src/theme/layout.ts`) from the header and from the left, right and bottom edges of the page; use that one value for all four margins (the header's bottom margin and the shell's padding) so they stay equal.
- The Activity Log is a drawer that extends from the bottom edge of the Table (`Table` renders it in `.table-shell`, beneath the board, so it never covers the seat controls). The icon button at the end of the dock toggles it. Whether it is open lives in `useActivityDrawer`: the `isActivityLogVisible` setting ("Open Activity Log by default") only decides the starting state, and applies at once when changed. Keep the drawer bounded to its fixed maximum height and scroll its entries vertically when they overflow, while keeping its heading visible and preserving horizontal table scrolling. While closed it must stay `inert` and `aria-hidden`.
- `useTableToasts` owns the toast timeline and paces the activity log. Toasts are a short running feed (`TableToasts`) rendered inside the dock, which anchors it just above the dock's top edge so the notices stay beside the buttons however far a tall board is scrolled; do not move it back to the top of the board. The Table renders two feeds from the one list: pot contributions (`isPotToast`, `kind: 'pot-contribution'`) go to `<TableToasts placement="pot">`, over the pot at the dock's start, and everything else to the feed above the middle of the dock. They share the hook's single queue, so the order and the pacing are unchanged; only the oldest-makes-way limit is counted per feed (`TOAST_MAX_LINES` for the table, `TOAST_POT_MAX_LINES` for the pot). Over the pot a line's subtitle (the pot amount) is visually hidden, since the badge shows it. `Table.css` positions the pot feed and, on a board under 1000px, lifts the table feed a line while a pot toast is showing (`has-pot-toast` on the dock) so the two never overlap, by a line for each of the pot's (`--pot-lines`). The pot is a button (`.table-pot-button`): tapping it shows the pot's breakdown in the pot feed in place of the contribution toasts, one line per player from `potBreakdown` in `src/functions/pot.ts` (the current hand's antes and wagers in the activity log, added up by player). `usePotBreakdown` owns its open, leaving and closed phases and reuses `TOAST_LIFE_MS` and `TOAST_EXIT_MS`; the feed gets `isFlat`, so its lines are not dimmed by age. Toasts arrive in order, `TOAST_GAP_MS` apart, and stay beside the lines already showing, newest at the bottom with older lines dimmer. Every toast gets the same schedule whatever its kind: it fades after `TOAST_LIFE_MS`, or sooner when more than `TOAST_MAX_LINES` are showing and it is the oldest, and takes `TOAST_EXIT_MS` to close up. The hook returns a change's log entries once the last toast of that change has been on screen for `TOAST_REVEAL_MS`; `ActivityLog` then slides the new rows in from above. Entries with no toast of their own wait behind the toast still due, so the log stays in order. At the end of a round each seat's result is a toast of its own (`kind: 'result'`, from `resultAnnouncements` in `src/functions/announcements.ts`, in turn order, the dealer last). Each holds the newest place for `TOAST_RESULT_MS`, during which its seat is the hook's `focus`, and the first waits out the dealer's hole card turn (`holdResultsMs`, from `useCardFlip`'s `waitMs`). `isAnnouncingResults` joins the pot and the card turn in `PotAnimationContext`, so Next hand and the other buttons wait until the last seat has had its turn. Keep `ACTIVITY_ROW_ENTER_MS` and `ACTIVITY_DRAWER_MS` in step with `App.css`, and cover timing changes with fake timers.
- Keep the in-app rules in `src/components/RulesDialog.tsx` and the README's Rules section accurate with the reducer/domain behavior. When blackjack rules or available actions change, update both descriptions and their relevant tests.
- Preserve the responsive table and seat behavior, and respect reduced-motion preferences when adding animation.
- Keep dealer automation in `src/components/Agent.tsx`; clean up timers and other effects when dependencies change or components unmount.
- Add or update colocated React Testing Library tests for user-visible behavior and accessibility-relevant changes.
